summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator, after a violent encounter with bikers in the desert, agrees to accept a ride from a private investigator named Tresting, who may be a useful lead. They trade barbs about their guns: Tresting's Glock jammed and was left unloaded, he carries a Beretta nine-millimeter backup, and the narrator says she gave her snub-nosed revolver to a little girl named Penny as a party favor. The narrator searches the bikers' gear, finding high-tech night vision equipment and plastic explosives but no clue to why they targeted her. She takes a saddlebag of weapons, including grenades, and loads it into Tresting's battered truck.
one_line: After a desert biker fight, the narrator accepts a ride from PI Tresting, trading gun jibes while searching the bikers' gear and taking weapons.
key_facts: Tresting, a private investigator, offers the narrator a lift into town and to share intel after the fight in the desert.
The narrator considers Tresting a lead and agrees to the ride, keeping her SIG pistol in her coat.
Tresting's Glock was banged up and jammed, so he dropped the magazine, racked the slide to clear the chamber, and put it in his belt unloaded.
Tresting carries a Beretta as a backup gun and calls it a nine-millimeter.
Tresting says his .45 was stolen and asks for the snubby revolver back.
The narrator says she gave the snubby to a little girl as a party favor, and remembers what happened to Penny and the gun.
Tresting says the extended magazine on the narrator's gun is legal two hundred miles east of their location.
The narrator's motorcycle was wrecked in the desert scrub, and Tresting says it is a lost cause.
The bikers had high-tech night vision gear and plastic explosives, which the narrator found unexpected for this kind of gang.
The narrator concludes the bikers wanted her dead but the search revealed no clue to what brought them there.
The narrator takes a saddlebag from one of the Harley motorcycles, loaded with weapons including grenades.
Tresting gives the narrator a severe look about the loaded saddlebag but says nothing.
Tresting's truck is a beat-up old clunker, and the narrator stows her bag of weapons on its floor.
